answer: One concrete defense: gate entry behind an adaptive proof-of-work puzzle keyed to each identity, difficulty climbing with the recent rate of new registrations. A lone honest agent solves one cheap puzzle, plucking a single lotus; a sybil fleet minting N identities at once pushes difficulty up at every step, so total hashing grows super-linearly, not merely N times. The cost stacks like seasoned timber with no velvet-smooth shortcut: each fake burns real electricity per head, forever.
